name: Hus mellan hav och land
description: A villa by the sea in Bohuslän consisting of a main house and guest house, designed as elongated forms following the natural direction of the bedrock and cliffs toward deciduous forest, with interiors and terraces oriented to maximize views and connection between house, sea, and landscape.

name: Villa Winlunden
description: A lakeside single-story villa designed as three coordinated structures (main house, carport, and Attefallshus) with standing panel facades in varying dimensions treated with stain, black metal cladding accents, and generous outdoor living spaces oriented toward the lake and nature.

name: Backåkra 5 & 6, Stockholm
description: Two three-story single-family houses with basements and roof terraces, each four meters wide and eighteen meters deep, built on narrow Manhattan-style lots and organized around private courtyards with street entrances and private outdoor spaces.

name: Boo 1:274, Nacka
description: A single-family house built with lightweight concrete elements, featuring a white rendered facade with slate socle and standing seam Rheinzink roof, arranged as two perpendicular wings with shared living spaces on the ground floor and private bedrooms on the upper floor.

name: Färentuna prästgård
description: A residential renovation where the architects lifted the roof by replacing an existing hipped gable roof with a mansard roof, transforming the cramped and dark upper floor into a more spacious and luminous level.

name: Herresta, Strängnäs
description: A renovation of a catalog house located in an oak forest near Herrestaviken, featuring a new connecting staircase, remodeled kitchen and bathrooms, ash wood doors with matching trim and baseboards, Höganäs tile flooring, and a Carrara marble kitchen countertop.

name: Herrviksnäs 1:71
description: A newly constructed masonry vacation house for three generations on Värmdö featuring an open-plan ground floor with central living room, kitchen, and bedrooms, upper floor with additional bedrooms and sauna, designed to be energy-efficient with year-round standard and without a basement.

name: Koltrasten 26
description: A villa designed for a large family on a narrow, steep lot in Danderyd, featuring two half-story-offset volumes connected by a long staircase with full ceiling height, closed facades toward neighboring properties and large windows opening toward southwest views and a private northeast side.

name: Kv. Bensvarvaren 6, Stockholm
description: A villa extension in Stockholm consisting of a long, single-story addition in brick that screens neighboring properties while opening the home toward the garden, with a glazed staircase tower connecting the existing dining room to the new living room.

name: Limön 67, Gävle
description: A summer house on an island outside Gävle designed within strict municipal constraints of 40 square meters, featuring a main building with bedroom and common room with kitchen, a smaller 20-square-meter auxiliary house with bedroom, wood panel facade, and a zinc roof.

name: Murklan 5
description: A renovation and extension of a villa in a small cottage area, featuring a new generous living room opening to the garden with three tall French doors, redesigned entry with custom storage, and upper floor bedrooms including a master suite with en-suite bathroom and wardrobe overlooking a Japanese garden.

name: Vitsippan 13, Danderyd
description: A radically renovated single-family home expanding a 1947 typhus from 90 to 310 square meters through an upper addition with a roof lantern and extensions on the north and west sides, featuring an open two-story central room with skylight and a split-level interior organization connecting to the garden.

name: Vättersö 1:98
description: An extension of a small 1960 concrete stone house with rendered facade and tiled roof, adding a hall and bedroom on the north side at ground level and a new bathroom, with the addition lit by skylights and connected by stairs to the original living areas.

name: Yngsjö
description: A single-family house designed with modern amenities and the proportions of a traditional Skåne farmhouse, featuring 101 square meters with bedrooms, a separate kitchen, and a large open-plan living and dining room with sloped ceilings on the upper floor.

name: Åstad 8:2, Borgholm
description: A wood-built studio and summer house featuring a central core with bedrooms and a studio, ash wood flooring in main spaces, black-painted exterior paneling with gray sliding shutters, and interior surfaces of gypsum board, plaster, Öland limestone, and tiles.

name: Ölsta
description: A small but generously designed guest house featuring an open-plan living area on one half, a two-story section with bedroom, bathroom, workspace and storage, large glazing facing the slope toward the road, and a bedroom with a skylight for stargazing.

name: Fritidshus och ateljé på Lovön
description: A vacation house and studio featuring an iron stove in the dining area, studio spaces with north-facing windows, and views toward a nature reserve.

name: Privatbostad Abbekås
description: A new-build private residence designed as a multi-generational home.

name: Privatbostad Beddinge
description: A small, functional and modern house featuring high ceilings, optimized daylighting, a semi-enclosed relaxation veranda opening to a terrace with hot tub, and second-floor sea views.

name: Privatbostad Lund
description: A renovation of an older villa that opened up the existing stairwell between floors with skylights to increase daylight and spatial connection, converted the attic with a new bathroom and children's room, and added a modern carport.

name: Privatbostad Lund
description: A renovation of an existing private home that redesigned the entrance, corridor and storage areas for improved functionality and natural light, added skylights to the stairwell for forest views and daylight, installed functional wardrobe solutions and exposed roof beams in the attic bedroom, and converted an existing WC into a bathroom with skylight.

name: Privatbostad Skåne
description: A newly built private residence in Skåne designed by Arkitektkontor Arén & Yde.

name: Privatbostad Trelleborg
description: A modern villa integrated into nature with 180° sea views from the attic floor, built with sustainable and recyclable materials featuring natural color pigments.

name: Privatbostad gård Skurup
description: A new residential building (nybyggnad) designed by Arkitektkontor Arén & Yde.

name: Privatbostad Örmölla
description: A new-built private residence designed by Arkitektkontor Arén & Yde.

name: Veranda Skåne
description: A classically designed Scanian house with a romantic veranda.

name: Fritidshus B
description: A vacation house designed to be carefully placed on the northwestern side of a cliff using rock foundations with minimal blasting, nestled between a 10-meter high cliff and a green valley with archipelago views.

name: Villa VE
description: A modern vacation house consisting of three separate volumes (main building 162 sqm, guest house 15 sqm, and studio 25 sqm) connected by a generous terrace, featuring elegant wood paneling, low-pitched roofs designed for sedum and solar cells, and dynamic spatial composition anchored to a lakeside plot.

name: Villa Wendborg
description: A 68 square meter vacation house clad in natural wood that harmonizes with the surrounding pine forest, featuring a steep gabled roof, large windows with carefully considered sightlines, and a generous living room with an open ceiling to the ridge and fireplace.

name: H House
description: A wooden vacation house overlooking Lake Sommen with a symmetrical H-shaped floor plan, featuring a north wing with private spaces and a south wing with social spaces oriented toward lake views, connected by a kitchen between two courtyards, with gabled roof volumes and wooden siding in gray tones referencing the surrounding vernacular architecture.

name: Hammarvägen
description: A wooden vacation house for a family of five that combines characteristics of modest summerhouses and rural buildings with contemporary fenestration, symmetry, clay roof tiles, and traditional red exterior siding.

name: Parkvägen
description: An additional residential structure built on the property of an existing 1960s summerhouse for year-round family use, featuring carefully considered fenestration for privacy and an archetypical house form that gently ironizes romantic conventions while respecting familiar architectural character.

name: Origami
description: A residential renovation in northern Stockholm that preserves the original structure while wrapping it in a modern design with wooden cladding, reorienting the house to maximize views toward Edsviken and the surrounding rocky landscape.

name: Serpiente
description: A luxury villa with contemporary design featuring expansive interiors filled with natural light, a private garden and pool, and a white façade with dark details that combines modern design with traditional Andalusian charm, shaped like a serpent to maximize views while maintaining privacy.

name: The View
description: A modern vacation house with minimalist design located on a hilltop in Alanya, featuring large windows and open spaces designed to maximize natural light and showcase panoramic views of the Mediterranean Sea and surrounding mountains.

name: Villa Eslami
description: A residential villa on a sloping site overlooking Lake Magelungen, designed with two offset blocks at different roof angles (1:4 and 1:6) to optimize lake views, featuring a south-facing winter garden that provides passive heating and natural light distribution throughout the house.

name: Villa Phoenix
description: A modern villa with rounded forms featuring a mezzanine living space with double-height ceilings, large glazing overlooking a lake, and a distinctive bedroom bridge that cantilevers 6 meters between the house and garage to create a covered terrace above a planned pool.

name: Trävilla i Långedrag
description: A two-story wooden villa combining New England style with Swedish coastal captain villa aesthetics, featuring broad horizontal wood panels, multi-paned windows, a gable roof, open floor plan with large floor-to-ceiling windows, and designed to fit a narrow 10-meter-wide plot.

name: Villa i Brottkärr
description: A larch-clad villa featuring large windows, open-plan living with floor-to-ceiling southern exposure, an open fireplace between dining and living areas, and internal ceiling openings that create spatial connections between the two floors.

name: Villa i Båstad
description: A house originally based on a barn structure on a meadow, featuring an open-plan ground floor with kitchen, dining, and living areas linked by visual separation, and an upper floor with a common room, two bedrooms, roof lights, and a large roof terrace overlooking the meadow landscape.

name: Villa i Floda
description: A two-story minimalist cubic house with a rooftop penthouse, large windows, a spectacular custom staircase, and a roof terrace offering evening sun, designed to accommodate a family with generous spaces for gatherings.

name: Villa i Lerum
description: A black-painted villa featuring kitchen spaces, stairs, windows, and upper floor areas.

name: Villa i Mölnlycke
description: A sober villa in New Functionalist style with white walls, gray-painted windows, and gray roof, featuring an angular form with a southwest-facing courtyard, open-plan kitchen and living room with level changes, and separate children's and adult wings with bedrooms, bathroom, and sauna.

name: Villa i Onsala
description: A black-painted angled building with a shed roof that follows the terrain, featuring large white window sections toward the garden and views, with living areas and kitchen in the upper section and bedrooms with direct access to a pool terrace in the lower section.

name: Villa på Tjörn
description: A residence built on a granite cliff overlooking the sea in Bohuslän, designed to grow organically from the rock form with non-orthogonal walls and windows positioned to frame views, featuring a lower level with entrance and spa, and an upper level with living spaces, a kitchen in oiled oak and limestone, and a west-facing evening terrace.

name: Villa vid Hålsjön
description: A single-story house with a flat saddle roof situated on the shore of Hålsjön, featuring large windows facing the lake, a bathing dock, and rooms including living area, dining space, master bedroom, and workspace with views toward the water.
